s01.text: Here is a strange fact about language models. The first token of any sequence absorbs a huge amount of attention.

s02.text: Not the important token. Not the last one. The first.

s03.text: And it is not about content. The first token gets the same treatment every time.

s04.text: The explanation is that attention needs somewhere to dump probability mass.

s05.text: Every head outputs a weighted average, and those weights have to sum to one.

s06.text: Early on, before the model knows what it is looking at, some probability has to go somewhere.

s07.text: So the model learns to use the first token as a sink. A place to put the leftover attention.

s08.text: This is not a quirk. It is load-bearing.

s09.text: StreamingLLM found that if you keep the first few tokens and slide the window, you can stream millions of tokens.

s10.text: But if the sink disappears, the attention collapses. The model has nowhere to put the mass.

s11.text: So the first tokens are not just history. They are the drain.

s12.text: Which is a strange thing to depend on, and an easy thing for a retrained model to lose.

s13.text: Keep the drain. Slide everything else.
